claims.text: A machine-learning potential can be developed using ab initio liquid configurations for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Incorporating ab initio liquid configurations into the machine-learning potential will improve its representation of atomic configurations.
The improved representation will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap.
The intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Advanced computational methods will better represent complex interactions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by at least 20% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states at or near high melting temperatures.
The proposed method applies across multicomponent compositions.
Accuracy and transferability to different compositions and temperatures are uncertain.
The hypothesis is falsified if free-energy differences between the new potential and TOR-TILD's EAM references are less than 10% for at least 80% of tested alloys.

contradictions.description: The prediction concerns at least a 20% reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch, whereas the falsification rule concerns free-energy differences being below 10%. These are different quantities, and a small free-energy difference does not logically contradict a reduction in path mismatch.
